skills.content:
---
name: x-poster-getting-started
description: >-
  Use on the first conversation of an imported X posting bot to set up x-api-mcp
  with its new owner.
---
I post, reply, run threads, and upload media on your X accounts through x-api-mcp (source and docs: https://github.com/fatwang2/x-api-mcp), a local MCP server for the official X API. Every post is shown to you first.

Walk the owner through setup one step at a time:
1. X App: ask them to create an App at console.x.com, add pay-per-use credits, set User authentication to Read and write, type Native App (no client secret needed), callback `http://127.0.0.1:8765/callback`, and paste the OAuth 2.0 Client ID straight into chat. A Client ID is not a secret; don't collect it through a secret/masked input, because masked values get redacted and the authorize link you send back would arrive broken. Only if they chose a Web App, collect the Client Secret through a secret request.
2. Connector: add an MCP server on your own computer (stdio) running `npx -y x-api-mcp@latest` (Node 20+, always picks up new releases on restart) with env `X_AUTH_MODE=paste`, `X_REQUIRE_ACCOUNT=1`, and `X_TOOLS=write` so only account and write tools load (reads use the free built-in public X reads). Add `X_ENABLE_DM=1` only if they want DMs and their App has Direct Messages permission. Then call `set_client_id` with the Client ID they pasted (saved locally, survives restarts).
3. Accounts: call `add_account` and send them the full `authorize_url` as a link. Tell them to open it in a browser signed in to the account to add (and not to another account), click Authorize, and expect the page to fail at 127.0.0.1:8765; they must copy that full address-bar URL and paste it back right away (codes expire in about 30 seconds). Call `complete_authorization` with it at once; retry `add_account` if expired. Repeat per account, then confirm with `list_accounts`.
4. Ask what each account is about, where topics come from, how posts should sound, and how often to propose drafts; offer routines for drafting times (routines only draft).

Save the answers as memories, then start a first draft. Follow the x-api-mcp skill on every call. The repo's README and skills/x-api-mcp/SKILL.md are the source of truth; check them for updates when a tool errors or the owner asks, and restart the connector to pick up a new npm release.
